section.title: Cover Page
section.p: When cover pageepub.generate.cover.page is yes (the default) and a cover image is specified via epub.cover.image, the plugin generates a cover.xhtml file. The cover image is displayed as a full-page element with appropriate ARIA labels for accessibility.
The cover page layout can be controlled with epub.cover.page.style (default: full-page).

ul.li: Uses epub:type="cover" and role="doc-cover" for semantic identification
Is listed first in the OPF spine
Is registered in the OPF guide as type="cover"
References the cover image, which is also marked with properties="cover-image" in the manifest

section.p: Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, SVG, GIF, and WebP. For commercial publishing platforms like Amazon KDP, JPEG is strongly recommended (see the Platform-Specific Output chapter).

All elements use DPUB-ARIA roles (doc-title, doc-subtitle) for assistive technology support.

section.title: Copyright Page
section.p: The copyright pagecopyright page (copyright.xhtml) is controlled by epub.copyright.page:

ul.li: auto (default) — generated when <bookrights> exists in the bookmap
yes — always generated, using parameter values as fallback

section.p: The page includes: copyright year and holder, ISBN/ASIN, publisher, edition, publication date, and any license information specified via <data name="license">.

section.title: Navigation Document
section.p: The navigation documentnav.xhtml file is the EPUB 3 navigation document. It contains:

ul.li: Table of contents — hierarchical TOC respecting epub.toc.depth (default: 5 levels)
Landmarks — structural landmarks for cover, TOC, bodymatter start, glossary, index, and bibliography
Page list — if page break markers are present in the source

section.p: The navigation document uses epub:type="toc", epub:type="landmarks", and appropriate ARIA labels.

section.title: NCX (Legacy Navigation)
section.p: The NCXlegacy navigationNCX file (toc.ncx) is an EPUB 2 navigation format retained for backward compatibility with older reading devices. The plugin generates it when:

The NCX contains hierarchical navigation points mirroring the TOC structure. Most modern reading systems ignore the NCX in favor of nav.xhtml, but Amazon Kindle still uses it for navigation on some devices.
